transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-14 15:00 PST | Duration: 46m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (Head of ML, Helion), Maya (Cloud Architect), Samir (Security Lead), Lena (CTO)

00:00 Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for taking the time. quick intro from our side - I'm Jordan, account lead, and with me is Priya who will go a little deeper on the network bits.
00:10 Alex - Helion: Thanks Jordan. I'm Alex, we run ML infra. We're investigating Private deployments of Redwood, mainly for PHI-ish model serving and data residency.
00:20 Jordan: Great, high level we'll run through options - hosted, dedicated, private - and focus on the VPC topology choices for Private.
00:35 Priya (Redwood SE): quick note, I might mention some infra terms loosely - I sometimes say KV cash instead of KV cache in calls, sorry in advance.
00:45 Maya - Helion: no worries. can you start with the connectivity options? We want minimal attack surface and no public internet egress for requests.
00:55 Priya: Sure. For Private you generally have two patterns: one is VPC peering / Transit Gateway peering where our service is deployed into your VPC or peered into it; the other is PrivateLink / private endpoints where you connect via interface endpoints and traffic stays AWS backbone. We also support Direct Connect/ExpressRoute with static routing for on-prem.
01:20 Samir - Helion: when you say deployed into our VPC, do you mean Redwood will run in our account as an AMI/container we manage? We need to understand control plane and data plane separation.
01:30 Jordan: Good question. For Redwood Private we offer two models: a customer-managed deployment (we provide an on-prem / private package you install into your account or cluster) or a Redwood-managed private tenancy where our control plane is still managed but the data plane lives in customer VPCs. We'll map those out after this call.
01:50 Priya: Right. In the customer-managed option, you host the runtime (we provide images and an operator). In the Redwood-managed VPC option, we spin up resources in your AWS account using a CloudFormation/Terraform bundle and we operate on the resources under an agreed IAM role.
02:10 Lena - Helion: For compliance we prefer customer-managed where keys never leave our KMS. Is that supported?
02:20 Priya: Yes. We integrate with customer KMS/HSM. In the managed option we can also bring-your-own-key; keys remain in your KMS and our services use a provided grant role for decryption at runtime. We'll capture detailed KMS flow in the whitepaper.
02:40 Alex: Region constraints — we're in us-west-2 and eu-west-1, and for data residency we need eu data to stay in eu. How flexible are region deployments?
02:50 Priya: We support deployments in most cloud regions, but some model variants and GPU families have regional constraints. For example, certain A100 nodes aren't in all regions. We can provision in your specific regions; if a model isn't available there we can offer a compatible variant or replicate inference endpoints in the desired region. This is a bit of a tradeoff between latency/cost and model parity.
03:20 Maya: If we use PrivateLink, do we need to open IGW/EGress for outbound requests to your control plane?
03:30 Priya: With PrivateLink (interface endpoints) the data path to the service stays on the provider's network; you still need to allow outbound to the endpoint ENIs but no public internet. For control plane callbacks (billing/metrics) we can route them over the same private connectivity or via an encrypted service endpoint—configurable.
03:50 Samir: Audit logs and syslogs — can we ship to our SIEM? We can't have logs retained in a vendor tenant.
04:00 Jordan: Yes, we can forward audit logs to your CloudWatch / Stackdriver / Azure Monitor or S3 bucket in your account. For Redwood-managed options logs can be exported on a schedule and pushed to your storage via S3 replication or cross-account role.
04:20 Alex: What about network NAT and egress IPs? Our security posture requires a fixed egress IP for allowlisting.
04:30 Priya: We can provide static egress through NATs or use fixed egress IP pools in the customer's account. With PrivateLink the outbound IP is the endpoint ENI, and for peering patterns you can NAT to an egress. We'll need your desired IPs/CIDR ranges to finalize.
04:50 Maya: Transit Gateway? We have multiple accounts connected via TGW. Can Redwood peer into TGW?
05:00 Priya: Yes, TGW is common. We can accept peering into TGW or establish a peering in the account where the inference VPC lives. For larger orgs we recommend TGW or Transit VPC patterns to avoid N peering relationships.
05:20 Samir: Encryption at rest and in transit — standard TLS for transit, right? But want to confirm data at rest is encrypted with our KMS keys.
05:30 Priya: TLS 1.2+/mutual TLS if requested for inter-service comms. Rest encryption is by default with provider-managed keys but we support customer-managed KMS keys for volumes and S3. We will include the crypto flow in the security doc.
05:50 Alex: Any restrictions on SGs or port openings? We run restrictive SGs.
06:00 Priya: For private endpoints we typically require TCP ports 443 for HTTPS and a few additional ports for health checks/metrics. For peered setups we rely on SGs and route tables. We can do IP-based or SG-based allowlists depending on the pattern.
06:20 Jordan: quick qualification — what's your expected RPS/throughput and latency SLOs for these endpoints?
06:30 Alex: We're targeting 200 requests per second avg with 50ms p99 for embeddings and ~150ms p95 for generation. Also need burst capacity during batch jobs.
06:45 Priya: Understood. We'll need to map model sizes, token counts, and batch sizes — that will determine GPU family and scaling profile. Dedicated pools can guarantee throughput; Private in-customer VPC can be sized similarly.
07:00 Maya: On the VPC CIDR side, we're using 10.0.0.0/16 in prod, some subnets reserved. Are overlapping CIDR ranges an issue?
07:10 Priya: Overlap is a blocker for peering; PrivateLink avoids that since it's interface endpoints. If you have overlapping ranges across accounts we usually prefer PrivateLink or route-based VPN translations (but those get complex).
07:30 Samir: For SOC2/ISO and audits we need vendor attestations and evidence of encryption, patching cadence.
07:40 Jordan: We'll send SOC2 Type II and ISO docs. For operational evidence, our Private offering includes patching schedules and optional maintenance windows coordinated with your SREs.
07:55 Alex: Can you do air-gapped on-prem? Some models will be trained with PHI data we can't send off cluster.
08:05 Priya: We do an on-prem package for fully air-gapped deployments. That path is heavier — we ship an operator, container images, and an offline bootstrap. It also requires local GPU infra and an offline license. We'll flag that as a separate engagement.
08:25 Maya: What about credential management for service accounts? We lock down IAM roles tightly.
08:30 Priya: We use an IAM role assumption model for Redwood-managed resources; for customer-managed we rely on your IAM and secrets manager. Short-lived credentials, roles with minimal privileges, and we support STS assume-role with a trust policy.
08:50 Jordan: A few common gotchas we see: 1) CIDR overlap blocking peering; 2) expecting public model variants in every region; 3) underestimating burst GPU needs. We can provide a checklist.
09:10 Alex: On billing and data locality — will billing records show model payloads or token counts? We need to know the level of telemetry sent.
09:20 Jordan: Billing is usage-based; we can provide token-level billing and can optionally strip payloads from reports. Telemetry can be configured to exclude raw inputs for privacy.
09:40 Samir: Any external IP callbacks for license checks or telemetry? We prefer none.
09:45 Priya: We can run without external callbacks; or callbacks can go to a private control plane endpoint. That is part of the configuration choices.
10:05 Maya: Walk me through a recommended architecture for us: non-overlapping CIDR, private endpoints vs peering, TGW?
10:15 Priya: Given your TGW + multi-account setup and requirement for no public egress, recommended pattern: deploy Redwood Private resources into a dedicated inference account/VPC, attach to TGW, and expose the endpoints to product VPCs via PrivateLink or via TGW route tables. This gives centralized management, fixed egress, and you keep KMS.
10:40 Alex: How long to stand up a pilot with a minimal model and run benchmarks?
10:45 Jordan: From sign-off we can do a pilot in ~2-3 weeks for a Redwood-managed private VPC in one region. Customer-managed on-prem takes longer (3-6 weeks) because of image transfer and air-gap steps.
11:00 Lena: For SLAs — do you offer uptime SLAs for Private?
11:05 Jordan: For Dedicated we provide SLA-backed throughput/uptime. For Private it's dependent on the chosen model: Redwood-managed private can have SLAs (negotiated) whereas customer-managed is covered by the customer's infra SLAs; we provide runbook and support tiers.
11:25 Samir: I want to confirm SSO and RBAC — we use SAML and SCIM for user sync.
11:30 Priya: We support SAML 2.0, SCIM provisioning, and granular RBAC for route and model access. Also audit trails for token usage.
11:45 Alex: Any limitations on model size for private installs? Large models require multiple GPUs and special kernel support.
11:50 Priya: We support large model sharding and quantized variants; however, very large models might require specific GPU setups. We'll need to pick the model family and discuss quantization tradeoffs.
12:10 Jordan: quick recap then next steps: we'll send SOC2 + security whitepaper, Priya will schedule a network deep dive and produce a sample architecture diagram and runbook, Helion will share CIDRs and region priorities, and we'll target a pilot in us-west-2.
12:30 Alex: Sounds good, thanks.
12:35 Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and the docs mentioned.
12:40 Meeting end.

Notes & references: Security whitepaper link (shared): https://redwood.example.com/security/helion-pack (note: placeholder). Network example diagrams will be attached to next email.

Transcript end.
